ruleName: Puddles and other abnormal course conditions
title: Taking relief from a puddle or abnormal course condition
question: Your ball is on the putting green and there is a puddle between your ball and the hole, affecting your line of play. What do the rules say you are allowed to do?

choices.text: Place the ball at the nearest spot where the puddle does not affect your line, no closer to the hole, with no penalty.
Try to avoid the puddle and play your ball as it lies.
Place your ball closer to the hole to find a dry line.
Take a penalty stroke and drop your ball anywhere on the green.

explanation: You are allowed to place your ball at the nearest point where the puddle does not interfere, not nearer the hole, with no penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What to do if there's a puddle on the green
juniorVersion.question: Your ball is on the green, but there’s a puddle in the way between your ball and the hole. What should you do?

choices.text: Move your ball to the closest spot where the puddle doesn’t block your putt, but not closer to the hole. No penalty.
Try to hit around the puddle and play your ball from where it is.
Move your ball closer to the hole to get away from the puddle.
Take a penalty and drop your ball anywhere on the green.

juniorVersion.explanation: You can move your ball to the closest dry spot so the puddle isn’t blocking your putt, but you can’t go closer to the hole. You don’t get a penalty for this.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The smooth area around the hole where you use your putter.
A small pool of water on the ground.
Extra strokes added to your score for breaking a rule.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children how to find the nearest point where their putt isn’t blocked by water and remind them not to move closer to the hole.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think they can move the ball closer to the hole to get a dry putt.
Some may believe they always get a penalty if they move their ball.
